source_review.notes: Checked current Google Spanner split, range, key-hotspot, schema, locality, and movement documentation; current CockroachDB range, replica, leaseholder, locality, and replication architecture documentation; and primary consistent-hashing, Dynamo, Bigtable, Spanner, Schism, and Calvin papers.

evidence: Defined keyspace, partition function/epoch, half-open interval, replica set, leader placement, virtual partition, hard/soft constraints, authority cut, hot shard, and hot key before use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Partitioning, replication, placement, routing, authority, and movement are kept distinct.

evidence: Recomputed interval routing at 0/99/100/999 and 599/600/700, upper child width 400, distinct-zone counts 3 versus 1, 600 MiB/(55-40 MiB/s)=40 seconds, and boundary mappings in Exercise 2.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Interval endpoints use explicit half-open integer semantics in the finite model.

evidence: Reviewed total/disjoint interval cover, split union preservation, snapshot-plus-delta move implication, per-failure-domain placement condition, and counterexample from uniform key counts to uniform request load.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Consistent hashing is not treated as a guarantee of bounded workload or safe state movement.

evidence: Reviewed lower/upper keys, gaps/overlaps, monotonic edge inserts, one hot key, shard-count change, stale router epochs, duplicate/gapped deltas, source/destination failure at every cut, one-zone loss, global-constraint conflicts, residency, full disks, and failure during rebalancing.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Once destination accepts authoritative writes, pointer reversal is rejected as rollback.

evidence: Checked exactly-one key ownership, versioned routing, legal replica placement, split/merge coverage, verified snapshot/delta cutover, local/global constraint scope, movement headroom, deterministic hot-key routing, and failure repair capacity; the finite fixture reproduced structural decisions.
invariant_checking.notes: Three process replicas are not accepted as three independent failure domains.

evidence: Reviewed half-open interval adjacency proof, split algebra, online move premises, placement survival predicate, and workload-skew counterexample.
proof_review.notes: Movement correctness remains conditional on complete ordered idempotent delta and one enforced authority cut.

evidence: Audited sharded, partitioned, replicated, placed, routed, split, merged, moved, rebalanced, hot, colocated, authoritative, fenced, globally unique, caught up, and verified terminology.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current vendor mechanisms are presented as examples rather than universal partitioning semantics.

evidence: CPython 3.14.4 reproduced the finite interval coverage/routing, split-boundary, movement-width, and zone-diversity fixture on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The fixture does not implement a database, directory, replication, consensus, migration, failure, residency system, or workload optimizer.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed range/hash/directory strategies, workload and key design, local/global indexes and constraints, replica placement, split/merge/move, dual-write hazards, rebalancing, hotspots, cross-shard operations, metadata/streams, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed online move cuts, routing cache epochs, owner fencing, quorum-preserving replica changes, bandwidth/log/disk headroom, rollback, source retention/deletion, failure-domain/residency constraints, noisy tenants, and fault injection.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives shard coverage and movement invariants from key ownership, supplies a passing finite model, ten distinct examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external database-vendor, distributed-systems, storage/network provider, security/compliance, operations, or production review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on key encoding/order, workload distribution, history and metadata epochs, snapshot/delta completeness, resource-enforced ownership, replication membership, failure-domain independence, constraints/index semantics, residency, capacity, implementation, configuration, and future version drift.
